</details>

#### How did you install `nvm`?
<!-- (e.g. install script in readme, Homebrew) -->
Internal distribution package

#### What steps did you perform?

In a much larger Ruby script:
```ruby
IO.popen(["bash", "-l", "-c", "nvm install v21.7.0"], err: :close, &:read)
```

#### What happened?

The 21.7.0 version was not installed

#### What did you expect to happen?

The 21.7.0 version to be installed

#### Is there anything in any of your profile files that modifies the `PATH`?
<!--  (e.g. `.bashrc`, `.bash_profile`, `.zshrc`, etc) -->

Yes, but it is not related


### My findings

The previous version we used (0.40.4) worked fine, and I bisected the issue to bda39c7c04ee0c34cad272fea3fc54e71f6ad710.
But it is *not* the actual culprit. It only activated the code path where the issue happening was reported.

My next debugging step was to check `stderr`, and it actually “fixed” the issue so I checked each patch chunk from the commit and without much surprise, the checksum step was the one that “failed”.

Since the issue appeared only when closing `stderr`, I checked any part of `nvm.sh` that would try to write to it.  
Commenting the `nvm_err 'Computing checksum with sha256sum'` and `nvm_err 'Checksums matched!'` lines from `nvm_compute_checksum` and `nvm_compare_checksum` indeed fixed my issue.

It is quite common in Ruby and other non-Shell scripting languages to actually close `stderr` (not redirecting to `/dev/null`) so I would consider a fix in `nvm_err` not to fail the entire operation when `stderr` is closed.

We will workaround with a `/dev/null` redirection for now.

#### How did you install `nvm`?
<!-- (e.g. install script in readme, Homebrew) -->
I'm using Debian Testing and WSL and I've installed nvm using the provided script in the README.md file, specifically with the following script, I've updated from version 0.40.5:

```sh
curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.40.6/install.sh | bash
```

#### What steps did you perform?
I've tried both in the Debian Testing branch and Ubuntu 24.04.4 (installed through WSL), in my .zshrc config I set the option `extendedglob` very early in the file, if I do so, when I load the shell, nvm does not automatically load the default node version I have specified in the default alias (to check it I've run `npm --version`, if node is loaded npm should also be loaded). This issue only occurs in nvm version 0.40.6 and did not occur in 0.40.5. Here's the .zshrc file I've used for testing the issue:

```sh
export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.config/nvm"

setopt extendedglob       # Extended globbing. Allows using regular expressions with *

# Temporarily turn off extendedglob if it's enabled
# [[ -o extendedglob ]] && local reset_eg=1 && unsetopt extendedglob

# Load NVM safely
[ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"
[ -s "$NVM_DIR/bash_completion" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/bash_completion"

# Restore extendedglob
# [[ -n $reset_eg ]] && setopt extendedglob
```

Using the above config, loading a new shell session and running `npm --version` returns the following error:

```sh
npm --version
zsh: command not found: npm
```

On the other hand if I temporarily disable the extendedglob option right before loading nvm using the following config for .zshrc:

```sh
export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.config/nvm"

setopt extendedglob       # Extended globbing. Allows using regular expressions with *

# Temporarily turn off extendedglob if it's enabled
[[ -o extendedglob ]] && local reset_eg=1 && unsetopt extendedglob

# Load NVM safely
[ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"
[ -s "$NVM_DIR/bash_completion" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/bash_completion"

# Restore extendedglob
[[ -n $reset_eg ]] && setopt extendedglob
```

nvm correcly loads the default node version I have specified:

```sh
npm --version
12.0.1
```

#### What happened?
In nvm v0.40.6 the zsh option extendedglob makes the nvm load script not load the default node version, this did not happen in v0.40.5 and does not happen if I disable the extendedglob zsh option.

#### What did you expect to happen?
nvm should be able to load the default node version regardless of if the option extendedglob has been enabled in zsh.

#### Is there anything in any of your profile files that modifies the `PATH`?
<!--  (e.g. `.bashrc`, `.bash_profile`, `.zshrc`, etc) -->
No, the testing has been done with a fresh zsh configuration using the files provided above, no .zshenv or .zprofile files have been used for testing, only the .zshrc files I provided above.

</details>

issue.title: nvm help "set-colors" legend never renders in color (command substitution defeats TTY detection)
issue.body:
### Summary

The color legend section in `nvm`'s default help output — the "Initial colors are:" line (showing `bygre`) and the "Color codes:" list — is **always rendered as plain text, never with ANSI colors**, on any terminal, with any `TERM` value, and regardless of terminfo availability. The rest of nvm's colored output (e.g. `nvm ls`) works fine.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run `nvm` (no arguments) in any color-capable terminal (`TERM=xterm-256color`, `xterm-kitty`, `screen-256color`, ...).
2. Look at the "Initial colors are:" / "Color codes:" section — it is plain text.
3. Compare with `nvm ls`, which is properly colored.

Minimal repro (after sourcing `nvm.sh`):

```sh
nvm_wrap_with_color_code b b           # -> ^[[0;34mb^[[0m   (colored)
echo "$(nvm_wrap_with_color_code b b)"  # -> b                (plain text)
```

### Root cause

In `nvm_help` (lines ~3496-3505 on master; 3285-3292 in v0.40.5), the color-wrapped strings are built **inside command substitution**:

```sh
nvm_echo_with_colors "  $(nvm_wrap_with_color_code 'b' 'b')$(nvm_wrap_with_color_code 'y' 'y')$(nvm_wrap_with_color_code 'g' 'g')$(nvm_wrap_with_color_code 'r' 'r')$(nvm_wrap_with_color_code 'e' 'e')"
```

`nvm_wrap_with_color_code` decides whether to emit colors by calling `nvm_has_colors`, which requires `[ -t 1 ]` (stdout is a TTY). Inside `$(...)`, stdout is a **capture pipe**, so `[ -t 1 ]` is always false and every wrapped token falls back to the plain-text branch. This section therefore can never show colors, on any system or shell.

Verified under both zsh 7.1.6 and bash 5.3.15 with the minimal repro above.

### Expected behavior

The `bygre` sample and the "Color codes:" legend should render in the colors they describe, like the rest of nvm's output.

### Suggested fix (for maintainers)

Make `nvm_wrap_with_color_code` not depend on `-t 1` when invoked inside command substitution. A simple approach: honor an already-computed flag like `NVM_HAS_COLORS`, which `nvm_print_alias_path` already does (see line ~1249: `if [ "${NVM_HAS_COLORS-}" = 1 ] || nvm_has_colors; then`). E.g. compute `nvm_has_colors` once in `nvm_help`, export `NVM_HAS_COLORS=1`, and have `nvm_wrap_with_color_code` accept that flag in addition to calling `nvm_has_colors`.

### Environment

- nvm 0.40.5 (Arch Linux package `nvm 0.40.5-1`); also present on current master
- Shell: zsh 7.1.6 and bash 5.3.15
- Terminal: kitty (`xterm-kitty`), tmux (`screen-256color`)

#### `nvm ls` output:
<details>
<!-- do not delete the following blank line -->

```sh
       v16.20.2 *
       v22.23.2 *
        v24.8.0 *
->       system *
default -> 24 (-> v24.8.0 *)
```
</details>

#### How did you install `nvm`?

Install script from the readme.

#### What steps did you perform?

Sourced `nvm.sh` (from `~/.bashrc`) in a Git Bash shell whose `$PWD` is Windows-style, e.g. `D:/Work` instead of `/d/Work`. This happens when Git's `bash.exe` is launched by a native Windows program (an IDE, a terminal, an AI coding agent, etc.). Bash keeps an inherited `PWD` if it names the current directory, and it arrives Windows-style:

```sh
$ cd /c && '/c/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe' --norc --noprofile -c 'echo $PWD'
C:/
```

Minimal repro, no files needed (wrapped in `timeout` because it never returns):

```sh
$ timeout 5 bash -c '. ./nvm.sh --no-use; PWD="Q:/a/b" nvm_find_up .nvmrc'; echo "exit=$?"
exit=124
$ timeout 5 bash -c '. ./nvm.sh --no-use; PWD="Q:/a/b" nvm_find_project_dir'; echo "exit=$?"
exit=124
```

Plain `. nvm.sh` hangs too, because the default auto-`use` (`nvm_auto use`) calls `nvm_find_project_dir`. Reproduced on v0.40.3 and on current `master` (b1b3a00).

#### What happened?

The shell hangs forever with 100% CPU, so every new shell in that environment freezes at startup.

Both functions walk up the tree with `path_=${path_%/*}` until `path_` is `""` or `.`. For a Windows-style path, the last step is `D:/` → `D:`. `D:` has no `/`, so `${path_%/*}` leaves it unchanged and the loop never ends. `set -x` shows it spinning:

```
+ '[' D: '!=' '' ']'
+ '[' D: '!=' . ']'
+ '[' '!' -f D:/package.json ']'
+ '[' '!' -d D:/node_modules ']'
+ path_=D:
...
```

#### What did you expect to happen?

The walk stops after checking the drive root (`D:/package.json`, `D:/.nvmrc`), like it does for a POSIX path like `/d/Work`.

#### Is there anything in any of your profile files that modifies the `PATH`?

Not relevant to the hang; it reproduces with `--norc --noprofile` as shown above. Workaround: source with `. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" --no-use` (note that an explicit `nvm use <version>` also hangs in this state).

#### Proposed fix

I have a fix with tests ready, and I will open a PR shortly. Stop the walk when going up doesn't change the path. This covers the drive root and also makes the existing `'.'` special case redundant:

```diff
 nvm_find_up() {
   local path_
+  local parent_
   path_="${PWD}"
-  while [ "${path_}" != "" ] && [ "${path_}" != '.' ] && [ ! -f "${path_}/${1-}" ]; do
-    path_=${path_%/*}
+  while [ "${path_}" != "" ] && [ ! -f "${path_}/${1-}" ]; do
+    parent_=${path_%/*}
+    # stop when there is nowhere left to go up, e.g. `.` or a Windows drive root like `C:`
+    [ "${parent_}" != "${path_}" ] || break
+    path_="${parent_}"
   done
```

The same change goes into `nvm_find_project_dir`. As with `.` today, the functions then return the place they stopped (`D:`). Both callers (`nvm_find_nvmrc` and the project `.npmrc` check) append a filename and test that it exists, so that's safe. The `""` check stays so that `/` itself still isn't searched on POSIX systems.

Tests: one case each in `test/fast/Unit tests/` (`PWD="Q:/nonexistent/dir"` → `Q:`), next to the existing `PWD="."` cases. Those new cases hang on `master` and pass with the fix in `sh`, `bash` and `dash`. I couldn't test `zsh` or `ksh` locally.

issue.title: Install script breaks last line in `.bashrc` if it doesn't have trailing newline.
issue.body:
#### Operating system and version: 
Ubuntu 26.04

#### How did you install `nvm`?
Ran install script: https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm/blob/v0.40.8/install.sh

#### What steps did you perform?
Run install.sh

#### What happened?
`~/.bashrc` got broken, the last line of the file ended up **suffixed** with `[ -s "$NVM_DIR/bash_completion" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/bash_completion"  # This loads nvm bash_completion`

#### What did you expect to happen?
Nvm content is added after existing bashrc content, regardless if the `.bashrc` has a trailing newline or not.

#### Additional information
It appears to only happen if the `.bashrc` already contains the line `. anything/nvm.sh` anywhere, so the install script triggers `=> nvm source string already in ~/.bashrc`. This is also a little odd, as the detection seems to be very generous in parsing any line containing `nvm.sh`, even if it's commented out

issue.title: nvm's shell hook adds ~250ms to every new zsh shell startup
issue.body:
#### Operating system and version:

macOS 27.0 (build 26A428), arm64 (Apple Silicon)

#### `nvm debug` output:
<details>

```sh
nvm --version: v0.40.8
$TERM_PROGRAM: Apple_Terminal
$SHELL: /bin/zsh
$SHLVL: 1
whoami: 'hridhinvarkeyjoseph'
${HOME}: /Users/hridhinvarkeyjoseph
${NVM_DIR}: '${HOME}/.nvm'
${PATH}: ${NVM_DIR}/versions/node/v20.20.2/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/opt/homebrew/sbin:/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.14/bin:/usr/local/bin:/System/Cryptexes/App/usr/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin:/var/run/com.apple.security.cryptexd/codex.system/bootstrap/usr/local/bin:/var/run/com.apple.security.cryptexd/codex.system/bootstrap/usr/bin:/var/run/com.apple.security.cryptexd/codex.system/bootstrap/usr/appleinternal/bin:/pkg/env/global/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin
$PREFIX: ''
${NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX}: ''
$NVM_NODEJS_ORG_MIRROR: ''
$NVM_IOJS_ORG_MIRROR: ''
shell version: 'zsh 5.9 (arm64-apple-darwin26.0)'
uname -a: 'Darwin 27.0.0 Darwin Kernel Version 27.0.0: Tue Aug 11 21:02:59 PDT 2026; root:xnu-13432.1.9~1/RELEASE_ARM64_T8142 arm64'
checksum binary: 'sha256sum'
OS version: macOS 27.0 26A428
nvm current: v20.20.2
which node: ${NVM_DIR}/versions/node/v20.20.2/bin/node
which npm: ${NVM_DIR}/versions/node/v20.20.2/bin/npm
```
</details>

#### `nvm ls` output:
<details>

```sh
->     v24.21.0
default -> 24 (-> v24.21.0)
iojs -> N/A (default)
unstable -> N/A (default)
node -> stable (-> v24.21.0) (default)
stable -> 24.21 (-> v24.21.0) (default)
lts/* -> lts/krypton (-> v24.21.0)
lts/krypton -> v24.21.0
```
</details>

#### How did you install `nvm`?

Homebrew (`brew install nvm`)

#### What steps did you perform?

1. With nvm's three lines active in ~/.zshrc (`export NVM_DIR`, and the two `[ -s ... ] && \. ...` sourcing lines), ran `time zsh -i -c exit` three times and noted the "total" time.
2. Temporarily commented out those same three lines in ~/.zshrc (backed up the file first).
3. Opened a fresh shell and ran `time zsh -i -c exit` three times again.
4. Compared the two sets of results.
5. Restored ~/.zshrc afterward.

#### What happened?

With nvm's hook active: 0.281s, 0.278s, 0.383s total (avg ~0.31s)
With nvm's hook disabled: 0.057s, 0.057s, 0.073s total (avg ~0.062s)

That's roughly a 5x slowdown — nvm adds about 220–250ms to every new interactive shell.

#### What did you expect to happen?

Sourcing nvm.sh should add negligible startup time.

#### Is there anything in any of your profile files that modifies the `PATH`?

Just the standard nvm-added lines in ~/.zshrc (added by `brew install nvm`'s setup instructions). Nothing else custom.

---

Searched existing issues for "zsh performance" / "slow startup" first — the closest match I found is #3410 (zsh initialization performance), tagged for this exact area but without concrete before/after numbers attached. Posting this with a reproducible measurement in case it's useful; happy to have it merged into that thread if preferred.
